advice: Propose a 64 KiB scratch buffer with half-band packing. For each 64-row band, pack 32 rows into scratch, process those rows across all 16 column panels, then pack the next 32 rows and process the same panels. Use a 128-byte scratch stride per K step, rewind 64 KiB after each reduction, and remove the second-half `scratch+128` address. This keeps all allocation and packing inside `gemm` and changes the measured 128 KiB scratch lifetime and traversal together. Hypothesis: halving scratch capacity may reduce stack-space pressure; the added packing pass and changed traversal may offset that benefit. No net gain is established. Check pointer resets and bounds, full output coverage, fresh-input correctness at tolerance 0.002, general sizes, tails, n<=0, and allocation-failure fallback. Then use the unchanged ten-report validation and ten fresh alternating paired controls, best-of-three rule, promotion gate, and held-out check. Compare against both the historical and fresh same-mode peaks without choosing the pending comparator policy.
risks: The traversal resembles the previously measured row-half-first experiment, which was not promoted; the smaller scratch and repacking make this a distinct combined change, but prior results do not predict its effect. More packing work may outweigh reduced scratch use. The complete timed path must be measured; do not attribute any joint outcome to scratch size alone.
